context: For (1) record a separate partition-key intent (or require BOTH catalog facts to match before upgrading to applied_verified). For (2) record the DDL directly after connection.execute(optimized) in create_schema() instead of deferring it through the post-load accumulator. Confirm against a live ClickHouse run that a partitioned+sorted table reaches the intended verdict and that applied_ledger_hash orders CREATE TABLE before OPTIMIZE TABLE.
description:
Two chatgpt-codex-connector review findings on merged PR #1275 (both P2, both in benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/workload.py). Deferred from the PR-review sweep in PR #1292 because each changes what counts as *verified* tuning and needs a real ClickHouse run to confirm; tracked in GitHub issue #1293.

(1) Partition keys are never corroborated. For tunings with BOTH partitioning and sorting (built-in ClickBench and TPC-DS table tunings), _optimize_table_definition() emits a single CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ..., but the recorded op is tagged only as sort_key. The generic corroborator then checks only system.tables.sorting_key and can upgrade the run to applied_verified without ever matching the configured partition_key, so common partitioned layouts report as fully verified with one catalog-backed key never corroborated.
Thread: https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/pull/1275#discussion_r3638089585

(2) Sort DDL is recorded out of execution order. create_schema() executes the tuned CREATE TABLE immediately, but the DDL is queued into _applied_layout_operations; the base adapter folds that list only after data validation, while apply_unified_tuning() has already recorded later OPTIMIZE TABLE statements. The order-sensitive applied_ledger_hash and its companion statement list therefore show the later optimize before the earlier table-creation DDL, so the ledger no longer reflects physical execution chronology.
Thread: https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/pull/1275#discussion_r3638089592

Note both fixes touch the same file, so they must land as one PR to avoid conflicting edits.

anti_patterns.dont: reorder the ledger by sorting the statement list after the fact
anti_patterns.instead: record each statement at the point it actually executes
anti_patterns.why: the hash must reflect real execution chronology, not a normalized order

anti_patterns.dont: upgrade a run to applied_verified when only one of the configured keys was corroborated
anti_patterns.instead: require every configured catalog-backed key to match, or record each key as its own intent
anti_patterns.why: that is exactly the over-certification this item exists to remove

preserves.behavior: A run with no tuned keys reaches exactly the verdict it does today
Untuned (notuning) ClickHouse runs still render engine-mandatory defaults only
applied_ledger_hash stays byte-stable for runs whose physical DDL did not change

verifications.description: ClickHouse tuning + workload unit tests pass

work_units.summary: Record a distinct partition-key intent (or require both partition+sort catalog facts) so a partitioned+sorted ClickHouse table cannot reach applied_verified on the sort key alone
Record tuned CREATE TABLE DDL at connection.execute(optimized) time so applied_ledger_hash reflects physical execution chronology
Verify on a live ClickHouse server that a partitioned+sorted run reaches the intended verdict and the ledger statement order matches execution
